Computes the observable support of a lifetime variable

retrieve_support.Rd

This helper function generates the observable supports of the lifetime and left-truncation random variables (Lautier et al. 2025, doi:10.1214/25-AOAS2103 ).

Usage

retrieve_support(Delta, m, omega, epsilon = NULL)

Arguments

Delta

a nonnegative integer denoting the period of time (in months) during which the ABS is marketed to prospective investors. It is after the trust closes to new loan originations but before its first reporting month.

m

is a positive integer representing the total number of months over which the underlying consumer auto loans are originated. This defines the length of the loan origination window before the trust closes.

omega

is a positive integer denoting the known, finite upper bound of a loan's lifetime (in months), which is nonrandom and observable from its amortization schedule at contract signing (for example, for a 72-month loan, we likely have \(\omega = 72\)).

epsilon

is a positive integer (default is NULL) denoting the present time (the current calendar month age since the first loan was originated) of the data generation process for an active ABS pool. If \(\varepsilon < \omega + m\), then right-censoring is present because it indicates some active loans are still making ongoing payments and have not yet terminated.

Value

A list with two integer vectors: X, the observable support of the lifetime variable (from \(\Delta + 1\) to \(\xi\)), and Y, the support of the left-truncation variable (from \(\Delta + 1\) to \(\Delta + m\)).

Note

The observed support may not extend all the way to \(\omega\) (omega). In that scenario, we set \(\omega\) to the age of the oldest active loan in the ABS bond (corresponding to \(\xi \equiv \min(\omega, \varepsilon - 1)\) in the notation used in Lautier et al. 2025), with \(\varepsilon\) denoting the present time.
